newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank seen pursuing stable crown.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank seen pursuing stable crown.

text.p: The Swedish crown has now appreciated to a level at which the Riksbank can feel quite satisfied, and the central bank's task in the future will be to maintain that level, analysts said on Monday.
"Quite simply, we think that the crown has found its proper level in value terms, and they (the central bank) want a rather more stable currency," Swedbank analyst Peter Lagerlof told Reuters.
The central bank said last week it would intervene more actively on the currency market to preserve the value of the crown, but not at any pre-determined level.
The Riksbank also said the interventions should not be seen as preparation for pegging the crown in the Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).
Analysts said that the Riksbank is likely to succeed in its stability aim with the government's far-reaching budget strengthening programme behind it.

"The deficit is under control, the current account is showing a surplus and growth is on the increase. This will by definition lead to a stable or appreciating crown," Beshara Mahdi of Morgan Stanley said.
The Riksbank would also avoid having to defend a specific level for the currency, analyst said.
"I think they will be very careful not to indicate any particular level," one economist said.

Even so, the Riksbank has given some indication of where it wants the crown exchange rate to be. In an analysis published in April, the bank said the crown's equilibrium value against the TCW trade-weighted index should be in the interval of 109 to 118 "with the emphasis on the lower half of the range".
The TCW index was 113.77 on Monday afternoon.
Another interpretation of the Riksbank's gambit is that it wants to gain the same room for manoeuvre as other European central banks.

"The Riksbank hopes to win the same ability to buy and sell currencies as other European central banks. This can be seen as a declaration of confidence in the crown -- it's so strong that it can even tolerate the Riksbank selling crowns," one chief dealer said.
Many economists believe that there is scope for a narrower spread between Swedish and German long bond yields following the Riksbank's comments.
The spread was around 190 basis points in April, but has fallen steadily to its current level of around 135 basis points.
"The way things look at the moment the spread could narrow to around 100 basis points in the longer term," Swedbank's Lagerlof said.
James McKay of U.S. investment bank Paine Webber agreed, but said German rates could constitute a risk.
"I think there is the possibility of the spread falling to 100 points, but the big test will be when we see signs of recovery in the German economy," he said.
Morgan Stanley's Beshara Mahdi is more pessimistic.

"In a situation with the crown outside the ERM, it's unlikely that the spread will fall further. On the other hand, if Sweden joins then there's a good choice of falling under 100 basis points," he said.
